question: Measure (not estimate) the /v1/graph coupled-honesty fix: real per-request DB query count and wall time, whether the per-type ceiling is silently firing, whether the phantom-drop ordering bug is live, and whether truncation_reason's literal value is a breaking client contract.
answer: MEASURED, and every figure is worse than the direction assumed. (1) PERF: 9,612 DB queries and 14.2s wall for ONE /v1/graph derivation over 1,927 docs / 52 schemas (local dev DB, telemetry-counted on [:barkpark,:repo,:query]) — the inherited '78 queries' figure is a ~123x undercount, not an undercount by a little. Breakdown: 4 queries for list_schemas, 420 cumulative after node listing (~8/type x 52 types, because list_documents re-resolves workspace/project/dataset per call), 9,192 in the edge phase alone (~4.8/doc: one list_schemas per document inside extract_edges plus one existence query per reference). Live guerrilla: cold 97.8s, warm 18.5-25.1s, 462,518 bytes. (2) The node listing runs TWICE — graph_corpus lists documents per type at tasks_controller.ex:943 and corpus_edges lists them AGAIN at edges.ex:655 — an unnoticed doubling. (3) SILENT PER-TYPE TRUNCATION IS LIVE NOW: the graph returns 998 task nodes with truncated:false while 3,137 published tasks exist (bp search facets) — 68% of the task corpus is missing and reported as complete. The limit:1000 ceiling fires, uniq_by drops 2, and NOTHING sets truncated. (4) The phantom-drop ordering bug is REAL but LATENT and IMMINENT: all_nodes = real_nodes ++ phantom_nodes then Enum.take(2000) drops the tail, i.e. the whole phantom layer first, while `edges` is never re-filtered against the kept set; live is 1809 nodes = 90% of the 2000 budget, so it is ~200 documents from firing. (5) types= is PROVEN silently ignored: graph_corpus(conn, _params) discards params, and ?types=paper returns a byte-identical 462,518-byte payload. (6) NO CLIENT BRANCHES ON truncation_reason's VALUE — it is display-only everywhere (graph.ts passes it through as a string, graph-landing.tsx puts it in a title= tooltip, core/types.ts types it string|null, and `node_budget` appears only inside comments). The vocabulary is therefore FREE to extend to per_type_cap/node_budget/both with no breaking change. One wiring trap: graph.ts:193 gates on `truncated ? ... : null`, so a reason emitted without truncated:true is discarded client-side. (7) bp-graph.js does NOT consume truncation at all — its `truncate()` is label-ellipsis text truncation, a false-friend grep hit. (8) There is a SECOND, WORSE twin: finder_live.ex graph_payload/1 is a verbatim copy of graph_corpus that Enum.take's to @graph_node_budget 2000 and emits NO truncated and NO truncation_reason field whatsoever — the LiveView finder cannot report truncation even in principle. Its own comment admits the duplication. (9) BASELINE: graph_controller_test.exs is 11 tests, 0 failures, and ZERO of them exercise GET /v1/graph (graph_corpus) — its describe blocks cover only /v1/graph/:id, /orphans, /dangling, /:id/tasks. 'The fix works' is currently unfalsifiable, as briefed. (10) PREMISE CORRECTION: there is no api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/graph_controller.ex — the action lives in TasksController, mounted at router.ex:1832 on [:api, :require_token]. The endpoint 401s without a bearer, so any anonymous graph probe is vacuous.
